overview.plainSummary: This bill changes how the federal government reviews and approves energy, mining and other building projects. It sets deadlines for environmental reviews, gives people 150 days to sue over a permit, and limits when agencies can cancel a permit already granted. It narrows parts of the Clean Water Act, Endangered Species Act and historic-preservation reviews, including how Tribes take part. It makes large data centers pay the grid costs they cause instead of other customers. The Congressional Budget Office’s preliminary estimate says the Senate version would add less than $1 billion to deficits over 2027-2036. S. 5653 is in committee; its text is moving as a Senate amendment to H.R. 2347, adopted 69-27 on November 18, 2026.
overview.valueWordCheck: No value words (sweeping, historic, radical, landmark, gutting) used.

considered.whyNot: Its written scope is emissions programmes, subsidies and rules, and it names "how long a project review takes" as out. The bill speeds wind, solar and transmission through permitting, which is permitting_reform. Emissions reductions claimed by supporters (RFF, 1.8 gigatons) are modeling, not text.

Chip: welcome data-center investment for jobs and tax base. No section offers an incentive. The text places costs on data centers (2107) and gives communities information (2117). The Evidence Locker's Heinrich items filed here are a pipeline read, not a text mapping.
Sec. 2117 (substitute) only has DOE inform communities about projected water use. It imposes no requirement, and the chip asks to "require".
Demand-side conservation key. The Clean Water Act changes (1202-1205) are permit scope and timing, held on permitting_reform.
Hydropower provisions concern generation licensing, not water-supply storage.

Runs both ways. Sec. 2211 removes a federal permit for owners drilling on non-federal land, strengthening the owner. Sec. 2101 widens FERC transmission permits, which carry existing Federal Power Act sec. 216(e) eminent domain, strengthening the government's hand. One support_meaning cannot hold both.
Its scope sends federal environmental review of projects to permitting_reform. Nothing changes general rulemaking procedure.
No federal land is sold or transferred.
Sec. 1304 delegates ESA consultation to States but transfers no land-management decision. Sec. 2212 concerns Tribal, not federal, land.
No new State cause of action against the federal government.
Cryptocurrency mining is one listed use of a computational load in 2107. The rule is about the load's grid costs, not digital-asset rules.
Data-center cost assignment is held by datacenter_power, its dedicated key. Filing it twice would double-count one provision.
Sec. 2110 has FERC consider AI tools in interconnection queues, a utility process rule, not tech regulation.
Neither text has wage, prevailing-wage, apprenticeship or labor-standard clauses (searched both). Labor endorsements are not text.
Div. C Sec. 3001 (substitute) is a narrow exclusion for damages on account of sexual acts, not a rate cut. Listed as an unmapped rider in provisions.
CBO's preliminary estimate is under $1 billion over 2027-2036. That is not a net fiscal direction large enough to read as a deficit vote, and it is shown as the scorekeeper finding instead.

Vocabulary gap. Secs. 2212, 2301 and 2302 change Tribal rights-of-way, Tribal historic-preservation programs and how cultural property is defined, and this is the most disputed part of the bill (see claims). No issue key covers it. Recorded here so it is not silently dropped; adding a key is a separate decision.

Neither S. 5653 nor S.Amdt. 6883 contains an abandoned-mine reclamation provision ("abandoned" appears 0 times in S. 5653 and only in unrelated contexts in the substitute). The nearest text is Sec. 2215's mill sites for waste rock and tailings, and Sec. 1602 brownfields.
